correspondence.RT-CPT-07: Apply the finite reduced crystallographic root-system results to V, the real span of the roots. Section 3 proves the hypotheses and identifies its reflection group with N_G(T)/T. The central complement is fixed; the torus case has V=0 and the trivial Weyl group.
correspondence.RT-CPT-10: Theorem 2.1 supplies integral positive-root expansions, Lemma 4.1 the simple-reflection permutation, and Theorem 5.1 and (5.2) the chamber and rho identities. Central directions remain separate. Coroot integrality does not replace the actual torus-period condition for analytic weights.
correspondence.RT-CPT-11: Sections 2–5 supply the same base, reflection and rho facts. Section 6 supplies the G2 roots. The consumer Gram matrix is twice the provider Gram matrix: the linear map taking each provider simple root to its consumer simple root has inner product multiplied by 2, so 2( beta, alpha )/( alpha, alpha ) is unchanged and this map intertwines each reflection. All six coefficient pairs and coroot coefficient pairs agree.
